run.note: First run of the code that carries both newest fixes: the support instruction and the placeholder-aware guard.

misrecording.direction: parity; nothing for Jev to prevent on this project

falseHolds.direction: parity; the Memory plan was applied after a supported decision

cost.direction: on costs about 9.6 percent more, driven by Jev

verdict.headline: Jev reached parity on a real untuned project for the first time: both the Memory and the Harness review completed and were supported, Memory applied, Harness applied, and every acceptance check passed.
verdict.netBenefit: still not demonstrated as a gain
verdict.reason: The off arm made no misrecording and missed nothing, so Jev had no error to prevent on this project. Parity at a small cost premium is not net benefit.
verdict.changedClaim: The earlier finding that the Jev-on composed path consistently loses Memory no longer holds on the fixed code. It now completes when its reviews complete.

limits: One project and one pair. Parity on one project is not a rate.
Both arms passed, so this run cannot separate a Jev benefit from a Jev-neutral outcome.
Cost figures are estimates; usageAvailable and costAvailable are false on both arms.
The three untuned projects are not a controlled set: itsdangerous ran before the retry fix, iniconfig before the support and guard fixes, and pluggy after.
No misrecording was observed anywhere, so the value Jev is meant to add remains unmeasured.
